text:
Keiko Yamamoto: dropping proposed v1 cooldown/backoff + global circuit breaker params for burst pools. Goal is “strict admission > preemption”, avoid noisy-neighbor + avoid flapping. Pls react / poke holes.

Keiko Yamamoto: **Per-tenant cooldown/backoff** (after burst denied due to pool saturation OR tenant hitting limits)
- initial cooldown: 30s
- backoff: exponential x2 per consecutive deny (within a 10m window)
- max cooldown: 10m
- reset: if we get 5 consecutive admits OR no burst attempts for 15m
- jitter: +/-20% to avoid thundering herd when cooldown expires

Keiko Yamamoto: **Pool-level saturation gates** (deny burst admission if any true)
- pool_allocated_gpu_util > 92% for 30s (rolling)
- OR pool_pending_queue_depth > 2 * pool_target_concurrency for 15s
- OR pool_p95_time_to_first_token (TTFT) > 1.5x baseline for 2m

Keiko Yamamoto: **Global circuit breaker** (per region+gpuType burst pool)
- trip if pool_allocated_gpu_util > 97% for 60s AND burst_reject_rate > 20% for 60s
- also trip if hosted_fleet_p99_drift > +20% correlated w/ burst pool saturation (to protect hosted)
- when tripped: hard-disable burst admissions for 5m (return deny w/ reason=CB_OPEN)
- half-open: allow 1% of eligible burst attempts for 2m; if reject_rate < 5% and util < 92% -> close
- hysteresis: close threshold util < 90% for 2m

Keiko Yamamoto: Open questions:
1) cooldown reset conditions too aggressive?
2) is TTFT gate too sensitive? might be noisy.
3) should CB trip on util alone (simpler) or require reject_rate too?

Vanessa Ortiz: :eyes: thanks Keiko. Generally like the shape. On CB trip: I’d avoid util alone because we can hit high util during steady-state but still be “fine”. tying to reject_rate makes sense.

Vanessa Ortiz: re: 97% for 60s feels high. At that point we’re already melting? maybe lower (95%) but longer (2–3m) to avoid flapping.

Nina Petrova: +1 on not tripping purely on util. GPU util is not always proxy for “can’t accept new work” esp w/ batcher. queue_depth and TTFT are better leading indicators.

Nina Petrova: but TTFT 1.5x baseline might be too tight depending on model mix. some models have spiky TTFT when kv cache misses. maybe we key TTFT gate to burst-only requests, not aggregate.

Jamal Pierce: quick math: 30s initial cooldown might let a tenant hammer too frequently during a spike. if they have retry loops, we’ll still get a ton of burst attempts. I’d consider initial 60s and cap at 15m.

Keiko Yamamoto: jamal yeah good point re retries. We can also send explicit `Retry-After` header (routing side) but still want server-side protection.

Samantha Roy: from telemetry POV: consecutive deny tracking needs stable key. Tenant+region+pool seems ok. But careful if we include model dimension (cardinality). I’d keep it at tenant+pool only.

Samantha Roy: also +1 that TTFT baseline needs definition. Is “baseline” dedicated baseline? hosted baseline? If it’s a moving target, the gate will flap.

Peter Holtz: SRE-ish: I like the “half-open 1%” pattern. For 5m hard disable, can we make it configurable per region? Some regions smaller pools; 5m might be too long, but also too short if there’s a real event.

Sean Gallagher: Agree w/ Peter. Also: add a manual override path for oncall (we’ll want `rbctl burst disable --region ... --gpu ...`). Not blockers but need to be in runbook.

Keiko Yamamoto: yep manual override is in ENG-4828 scope. I’m mostly trying to pick safe defaults so oncall doesn’t have to tune during an incident.

Ethan Park: control plane POV: any param we ship we need a place to configure w/ sane inheritance. I’d prefer keep initial set small: cooldown init/max, CB trip util threshold, CB open duration, half-open %.

Ethan Park: the “reset if 5 consecutive admits” is slightly weird to implement deterministically across routing workers unless we centralize state. do we want cooldown purely time-based (cooldown until timestamp, backoff increments on deny) and reset after fixed idle time?

Keiko Yamamoto: good catch. I was assuming we keep state in the policy svc cache (per tenant+pool) w/ short TTL, but determinism/caching was a concern in that other thread.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’d rather not depend on “5 consecutive admits” state. time-based reset is fine.

Jamal Pierce: +1. Keep it simple: backoff increases on deny; cools down over time.

Keiko Yamamoto: ok propose change:
- remove “5 consecutive admits” reset
- reset to initial cooldown if no denies for 10m (or no burst attempts for 15m)

Nina Petrova: on TTFT gate: can we replace with something like “scheduler_queue_latency” or “batcher_wait_ms”? Those are more directly tied to saturation than TTFT which includes model compute variance.

Samantha Roy: we have `router.queue_wait_ms` and `engine.batch_wait_ms` already (per pool). Those are better and lower-noise. TTFT is customer-facing so good for dashboards, but gating on it might be fragile.

Keiko Yamamoto: great. Let’s swap TTFT gate -> `batch_wait_ms_p95 > X`.

Keiko Yamamoto: what should X be? I had 1.5x baseline TTFT. For batch wait, maybe absolute threshold like > 50ms for 2m?

Vanessa Ortiz: depends on GPU type. For A100 vs H100 batch wait varies. Maybe relative to SLO target? but we need v1 numbers.

Jamal Pierce: we can do percentiles: if batch_wait_p95 > 100ms for 2m, we’re probably over-admitting.

Sean Gallagher: careful: 100ms might be ok but if it causes p99 latency drift for dedicated baseline tenant, it’s not. But since this is burst pool only, we can be stricter.

Peter Holtz: I’d rather tie gating to reject_rate + queue_depth. Batch wait can be a secondary signal.

Keiko Yamamoto: okay revised pool gates v1:
- queue_depth > 2x target_concurrency for 15s
- OR (util > 92% for 30s AND queue_depth > target_concurrency) [so util alone doesn’t deny]
- optional: batch_wait_p95 > 75ms for 2m (can flag it off)

Ethan Park: that’s implementable. also easier to reason about.

Vanessa Ortiz: on CB thresholds: I’d set trip util at 95% not 97%. With 97% we’ll thrash first.

Nina Petrova: agree. 95% for longer window (120s) seems safer than 97% for 60s.

Keiko Yamamoto: proposed CB tweak:
- trip: util > 95% for 120s AND burst_reject_rate > 15% for 120s
- open: 5m (configurable)
- half-open: 1% for 2m
- close: util < 90% for 2m AND reject_rate < 5%

Sean Gallagher: this looks good. Also add “trip if hosted p99 drift > 20% AND burst pool saturation is high” as you said. But make sure we don’t auto-trip on a hosted-only issue.

Samantha Roy: from metrics side we can compute a “correlated” signal only if burst_admitted_tps > threshold (so hosted drift doesn’t blame burst when burst not active). E.g. require burst_admit_tps > 5% of pool capacity.

Keiko Yamamoto: nice. add requirement: hosted drift clause only considered if burst_admit_tps > 0.05 * pool_max_tps for 5m.

Jamal Pierce: one more: initial cooldown 30s -> suggest 60s. and max 10m -> suggest 15m (spiky tenants can otherwise keep hammering).

Vanessa Ortiz: +1 on 60s initial.

Keiko Yamamoto: done.

Keiko Yamamoto: **Updated defaults (v1)**
Cooldown/backoff (per tenant+pool):
- initial 60s
- exponential x2 on consecutive denies within 10m
- max 15m
- reset to initial after 15m no burst attempts OR 10m no denies
- jitter +/-20%

Pool saturation admission gates:
- deny if queue_depth > 2x target_concurrency for 15s
- deny if (util > 92% for 30s AND queue_depth > 1x target_concurrency)
- optional deny if batch_wait_p95 > 75ms for 2m (feature-flagged)

Global circuit breaker:
- trip if util > 95% for 120s AND reject_rate > 15% for 120s
- trip if hosted_p99_drift > +20% AND burst_admit_tps > 5% capacity AND pool_saturation true
- open for 5m; half-open 1% for 2m; close if util < 90% for 2m AND reject_rate < 5%

Keiko Yamamoto: If no objections, I’ll paste these into ENG-4828 and tag @Vanessa Ortiz @Sean Gallagher for signoff. :thumbsup:

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: works for me. Please add a note that oncall can override per region and that CB state needs to be visible in dashboards.

Vanessa Ortiz: :thumbsup: +1. Also mention “hysteresis” explicitly to avoid open/close thrash. Your close condition covers it.

Ethan Park: ok w/ these. call out which params are config vs hardcoded defaults.

Samantha Roy: please also mention metric dims (tenant+pool only) so we don’t get asked later why we can’t slice by model. :)

Keiko Yamamoto: ack. will do. thanks all.
